record.field: Standard SLA for service providers – defines uptime, response times and KPIs.

Service Level Agreement

This Service Level Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into between {{client_name}} ("Client") and {{service_provider_name}} ("Service Provider") effective from {{effective_date}}.

The Service Provider shall render the services described in this Agreement and its annexures, subject to the required service levels, governance and reporting obligations.

This Agreement remains valid for {{contract_term_months}} months unless terminated in accordance with the termination clause.

Scope of Work

The Service Provider shall deliver the following services in accordance with the agreed Service Level Agreement:

  1. Maintain continuous service availability in line with the agreed uptime targets.
  2. Respond to incidents within stipulated response times:
    • Priority 1 (Critical): 1 hour
    • Priority 2 (High): 4 hours
    • Priority 3 (Medium): 24 hours
    • Priority 4 (Low): 72 hours
  3. Submit monthly performance/availability reports to the Contract Manager by the 5th of each month.
  4. Maintain suitably qualified and experienced personnel for the full duration of the agreement.
  5. Ensure data security, confidentiality and integrity in compliance with POPIA and applicable information security standards.
  6. Attend quarterly service review meetings with the Client's designated representative.

Terms of Reference (TOR) — Service Level Agreement

1. Background

The Client requires reliable and measurable service delivery standards with clearly defined performance outcomes and accountability mechanisms.

2. Objectives

  • Define minimum service levels and measurable performance metrics.
  • Establish clear accountability structures and escalation procedures.
  • Govern reporting, monitoring and remediation processes.

3. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Performance shall be measured monthly against KPIs agreed between the Parties and annexed to this agreement as Annexure A – KPI Schedule.

4. Penalties & Service Credits

Non-compliance with agreed service levels shall attract penalties / service credits as stipulated in Annexure B – Penalty Schedule. Cumulative non-compliance may lead to contract termination with 30 days' notice.

5. Change Management

Changes to service scope, KPIs or performance thresholds shall be effected by written amendment signed by both Parties.

6. Dispute Resolution

Any dispute arising from this agreement shall first be subjected to internal negotiation (30 days), and failing that, to independent mediation in terms of the applicable legislation.
General professional services agreement for consultants, contractors and specialists.

Service Agreement

This Service Agreement is concluded between {{client_name}} and {{service_provider_name}} for professional services effective from {{effective_date}}.

The service fee shall be {{contract_value}} and payment shall be made in accordance with agreed milestones and valid tax invoices.

The Parties agree to perform their obligations in good faith and in compliance with applicable laws and policies.

Scope of Work

The Service Provider is appointed to render the following professional services to the Client:

  1. Conduct a needs assessment and deliver a detailed implementation plan within 30 calendar days of commencement.
  2. Provide all labour, materials, equipment and expertise necessary for successful and timely delivery.
  3. Liaise with the designated Client representative(s) on a weekly basis or as otherwise agreed.
  4. Submit written progress reports on a monthly basis, or at agreed intervals.
  5. Obtain prior written approval from the Client before entering into any sub-contracting arrangements.
  6. Ensure quality assurance measures are in place throughout the duration of the contract.

Terms of Reference (TOR) — Service Agreement

1. Background & Rationale

This agreement governs the provision of professional services by the Service Provider to the Client for the duration specified in the contract header.

2. Deliverables

  • Inception Report (within 15 days of commencement)
  • Monthly Progress Reports
  • Draft Final Report (for Client comment)
  • Final Deliverable / Project Completion Report

3. Duration

Services shall be rendered for the period specified in this agreement, unless earlier terminated or extended by mutual written agreement.

4. Governance & Compliance

All work shall comply with applicable national legislation, municipal by-laws and the Client's Supply Chain Management Policy.

5. Intellectual Property

All deliverables, reports and outputs produced under this agreement shall vest in the Client upon full payment, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

6. Liability

The Service Provider shall maintain professional indemnity insurance appropriate to the nature of services rendered for the duration of this agreement.
Funding / grant disbursement agreement for recipient organisations.

Funding Agreement

This Funding Agreement is entered into between {{funder_name}} ("Funder") and {{recipient_name}} ("Recipient") effective on {{effective_date}}.

The Funder approves a total grant amount of {{grant_amount}} for the approved programme, subject to the terms and reporting requirements in this Agreement.

The Recipient shall only use funds for approved purposes and comply with all applicable regulatory requirements.

Scope of Work

The Recipient Organisation shall utilise the funding exclusively for the following approved purposes:

  1. Implement the programme / project described in the approved Business Plan (Annexure A).
  2. Maintain accurate and complete financial records; submit quarterly financial statements to the Funder within 30 days of each quarter-end.
  3. Permit the Funder or its authorised representatives to conduct audits, inspections and site visits at any reasonable time with 5 working days' notice.
  4. Report on programme outcomes against agreed indicators, targets and milestones.
  5. Return any unspent funds (with supporting reconciliation) to the Funder at the end of the funding period.
  6. Acknowledge the Funder's contribution in all communications, publications and public events related to the funded programme.

Terms of Reference (TOR) — Funding Agreement

1. Purpose of Funding

Funds are disbursed to support the implementation of approved community development / service delivery initiatives as outlined in the approved project plan and budget.

2. Conditions of Grant

  • Funds must be used strictly for approved purposes and in accordance with the approved budget.
  • Any variation exceeding 10% of a budget line item requires prior written approval from the Funder.
  • Receipts, invoices and supporting documentation must be retained for a minimum of 5 years post-project.
  • The funded organisation must not divert funds to activities not covered by this agreement.

3. Reporting Requirements

Quarterly narrative and financial reports are due within 30 days of each quarter-end. A final evaluation report shall be submitted within 60 days of project completion.

4. Compliance

The Recipient shall comply with the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA), Municipal Finance Management Act (MFMA), and all applicable legislation governing the use of public funds.

5. Termination & Recovery

The Funder reserves the right to suspend or terminate funding and recover disbursed amounts in the event of material breach, misappropriation of funds, or persistent failure to report.

Memorandum of Understanding

This Memorandum of Understanding is made between {{party_a_name}} and {{party_b_name}} to formalise areas of collaboration from {{effective_date}}.

The Parties will collaborate on jointly identified initiatives and maintain regular governance meetings to monitor implementation.

This MOU is valid for {{mou_term_years}} years unless terminated earlier by written notice.

Scope of Cooperation

The Parties agree to cooperate in the following areas for the mutual benefit of both organisations and the communities they serve:

  1. Share relevant information, data and resources in support of mutually agreed objectives.
  2. Designate liaison officers responsible for day-to-day coordination between the Parties.
  3. Conduct joint planning and review sessions at least twice per annum.
  4. Develop and implement joint programmes or initiatives as agreed in writing by both Parties.
  5. Review the MOU annually and amend by mutual written agreement where circumstances require.
  6. Coordinate communications to present a unified public message on areas of joint cooperation.

Terms of Reference (TOR) — Memorandum of Understanding

1. Nature of Agreement

This MOU records the intentions and commitments of the Parties to cooperate in pursuit of shared objectives. It is not intended to be a legally binding commercial contract but represents the good faith of both Parties.

2. Responsibilities

  • Each Party shall appoint a dedicated relationship manager / focal point.
  • Costs incurred by each Party in fulfilling their obligations shall be borne by that Party unless otherwise agreed in writing.
  • Neither Party shall commit the other to financial obligations without prior written consent.

3. Duration

This MOU shall remain in force for a period of 3 years from the date of signature, unless extended by mutual written agreement or terminated earlier by either Party on 30 days' written notice.

4. Confidentiality

Both Parties agree to maintain the confidentiality of sensitive information shared under this MOU in compliance with applicable law, including POPIA.

5. Dispute Resolution

The Parties shall endeavour to resolve any disagreement amicably through good-faith engagement before resorting to formal dispute resolution processes.
On-call professional retainer for specialists, legal counsel, etc.

Retainer Agreement

This Retainer Agreement is entered into by {{client_name}} and {{consultant_name}} effective from {{effective_date}}.

The Consultant is appointed on a monthly retainer of {{monthly_retainer_fee}} for up to 40 billable hours per month, excluding approved out-of-scope services.

All services will be rendered professionally and in accordance with agreed turnaround times and reporting obligations.

Scope of Work

The Consultant is retained on a monthly basis to provide the following on-call professional services:

  1. Provide specialist advice and written recommendations upon request, within agreed response times.
  2. Attend meetings, workshops, hearings and site visits as required by the Client (maximum 5 days per month inclusive).
  3. Review, advise on and draft documents, reports, legal instruments and correspondence referred by the Client.
  4. Maintain availability during normal business hours (08:00–17:00, Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays).
  5. Prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports within agreed turnaround times.
  6. Disclose and manage any actual or perceived conflicts of interest promptly.

Terms of Reference (TOR) — Retainer Agreement

1. Retainer Basis

The Consultant is engaged on a monthly retainer basis. The monthly retainer fee covers a maximum of 40 billable hours per month. Hours in excess thereof shall be invoiced at the agreed hourly rate as per Annexure A – Fee Schedule.

2. Scope Limitations

Services outside the agreed retainer scope require a separate written instruction and additional fee arrangement before commencement.

3. Exclusivity

Unless otherwise agreed in writing, this retainer is non-exclusive and the Consultant may provide similar services to other clients, provided there is no conflict of interest with the Client's interests.

4. Invoicing

The Consultant shall submit monthly tax invoices by the last working day of each month, accompanied by a schedule of work and time performed during that month.

5. Termination

Either Party may terminate this agreement with 30 calendar days' written notice. The Client shall pay for all work performed up to the effective date of termination.
Property or asset sale and transfer agreement.

Deed of Sale

This Deed of Sale is entered into by {{seller_name}} ("Seller") and {{purchaser_name}} ("Purchaser") on {{effective_date}}.

The Seller sells and the Purchaser purchases the property / asset described in Annexure A for a purchase price of {{purchase_price}}, subject to agreed conditions precedent.

Transfer and registration shall proceed in accordance with this Agreement and applicable conveyancing requirements.

Scope of Transaction

The Seller agrees to sell, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase, the property / asset described in this agreement on the following basis:

  1. Transfer of ownership of the property / asset as described in Annexure A – Property Schedule.
  2. The Seller warrants that the property is free from encumbrances, liens and third-party claims, save as disclosed herein.
  3. The Purchaser shall take possession on the date of registration / payment of the full purchase consideration.
  4. All risk in and benefit from the property shall pass to the Purchaser on the date of possession.
  5. Transfer costs shall be borne by the Purchaser unless otherwise agreed.

Terms of Reference (TOR) — Deed of Sale

1. Purchase Consideration

The purchase price is as stated in this agreement and shall be payable in the manner described in Clause 4 – Payment Terms.

2. Conditions Precedent

  • This sale is subject to the conditions precedent listed in Annexure B, which must be fulfilled within the stipulated period.
  • Should any condition not be fulfilled in time, either Party may elect to waive it (if capable of waiver) or cancel the agreement.

3. Voetstoots

The property is sold voetstoots (as-is). The Seller discloses all known latent and patent defects in Annexure C – Disclosure Schedule.

4. Transfer & Registration

Transfer shall be attended to by the Conveyancers nominated by the Client as soon as practicable after fulfilment of all conditions precedent and payment of the purchase price.

5. Breach

Should either Party breach this agreement and fail to remedy such breach within 7 days of written notice, the innocent Party may cancel the agreement and claim damages.
